b: Thousands of tabletop gaming enthusiasts and industry professionals are set to descend on Philadelphia next week for PAX Unplugged, with this year’s event bringing together publishers, designers, artists and other industry figures for three days of new games, panel discussions and networking.

The convention, running from December 4 to 6 at the Pennsylvania Convention Center, will feature sessions aimed at current and aspiring tabletop industry professionals, covering everything from making the leap into a career in games and commissioning professional artwork to pitching designs and getting feedback on unpublished prototypes.

There will also be opportunities to meet the leadership of the Tabletop Game Designers Association, work alongside established industry professionals on new designs and discover independent games being sold outside traditional publishing and crowdfunding channels.
BoardGameWire has rounded up some of the most interesting-looking talks, workshops and networking events for tabletop industry professionals across the three days.

Board game designers looking to test their latest prototypes can get feedback from players throughout PAX Unplugged through a series of playtesting sessions organised by Unpub. Designers can reserve tables in advance for a fee, giving them an opportunity to put their games in front of potential players, identify problems and refine their designs ahead of publication or pitching to publishers. Attendees interested in trying unpublished games can participate for free, with no advance registration required. Player seats are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.
Details of table reservations are available through Unpub’s website.
Offers & Asks: A Creators Networking Event

A structured networking event aimed at helping tabletop designers and other industry professionals find potential collaborators, based on the skills and resources they can offer and the help they’re looking for. Attendees are asked to arrive with two things in mind – a skill, idea or resource they could offer someone else, and something they would like help developing. These are posted on communal ‘offers’ and ‘asks’ boards, allowing participants to identify people whose skills and goals complement their own. The format is designed to help participants find useful professional connections rather than relying on chance encounters around the convention.

Five tabletop industry professionals discuss how they made the transition from careers outside the games industry to making a living from designing, publishing and developing games, including the risks, challenges and lessons learned along the way. The panel features Burnt Island Games and KTBG’s Helaina Cappel, Finspan and LEGO Monkey Palace designer David Gordon, Cardboard Alchemy’s Peter Vaughn, Flatout Games’ Molly Johnson and Roxley Games director of operations Kira Peavley. The discussion will explore how the panellists balanced other jobs with their early games industry work, what prompted them to make the switch, and how their professional lives have developed since.

Board game designers, artists, editors and other tabletop industry creatives can meet fellow professionals and the leadership of the Tabletop Game Designers Association (TTGDA) at this free networking event. The meetup offers an opportunity to discuss experiences working in the industry, make new professional connections and learn about the association’s services and support for tabletop creators. TTGDA representatives attending will include Wingspan designer Elizabeth Hargrave and Pandemic creator Matt Leacock, with attendees invited to ask questions about the organisation and its work. The event is open to TTGDA members and non-members alike.

Board game designers can watch industry professionals evaluate pitches for unpublished games at this live feedback session organised by Unpub. Participating designers will have six minutes each to present their games to a panel of industry professionals, before receiving feedback on both their pitches and the games themselves. The event offers aspiring designers an opportunity to see how experienced industry figures assess new game concepts, identify potential weaknesses and respond to pitches – even if they aren’t presenting a game themselves. Audience seating is free and does not require advance registration, although attendees will need to join a queue before the event begins.
That’s not how it happened! Historical Representation in Games

Designers and publishers working on historical games can explore the challenges of balancing historical accuracy with engaging gameplay at this panel featuring historians and academics. The discussion will examine questionable representations of historical events and figures in wargames and tabletop RPGs, including when designers should prioritise historical accuracy and where they might reasonably depart from it for storytelling or gameplay purposes. Speakers include University of Massachusetts historian Hadeel Jeanne, Dr Amelia Herbst of Respec Psychological Services and Kelly McManus of 20 Sided Gamified.
These Games Are Not For Sale

Not every game is designed to become a commercial product. This panel explores the possibilities of making games as personal, artistic or experimental projects, rather than with publication or retail sales in mind. Led by Tony Tran and Gene Koo, the discussion will feature designers including Pandemic creator Matt Leacock, exploring how games can be developed around personal, artistic and experimental goals rather than commercial considerations. Several participating designers will also be presenting games created as unique, temporary experiences for PAX Unplugged throughout the weekend, in a dedicated area of the Terrace Ballroom on Level 4, alongside the First Look and Unpub playtesting areas.

Publishers looking for new ideas can discover games from 26 independent designers at this marketplace organised by PAX Unplugged and New Mill Industries. The event will feature unsigned games that have not been crowdfunded, giving their creators an opportunity to sell directly to attendees when they have no other established sales channel. Only games will be available to purchase, rather than artwork, merchandise or accessories, with each designer operating their own queue. Further details are available on the New Mill Industries website. Sales begin at 7pm, with organisers asking attendees not to queue before the event starts.
Break My Game Community Meet-up and Playtesting

Board game designers can meet fellow creators and take part in informal playtesting at this gathering organised by the Break My Game community. The event offers an opportunity to exchange feedback on games in development and learn more about the organisation’s activities. The meetup is open to existing community members and anyone interested in joining.

Aspiring board game designers can work alongside industry professionals to create a new game from scratch in about an hour at this collaborative design event organised by Unpub. Participants will be divided into teams, each led by an industry professional, and challenged to develop a game around a randomly generated set of restrictions covering elements such as theme, components and mechanics. Teams will then present their designs to the other participants, comparing how different groups approached the creative constraints. The session will feature Unpub’s Benjamin Begeal.

Publishers, designers and other tabletop creators looking to commission original artwork can learn how to find and work with professional artists, including navigating commercial rights, compensation, client etiquette and managing expectations on both sides of the relationship. The panel will also explore commissioning human artists as an alternative to generative AI, with advice on communicating creative requirements and building productive working relationships. Speakers include illustrator and art director Nala J. Wu, character designer and author Rebecca Gray, and author Jarrod Taylor, with Stephen Myers moderating.
The full programme of events at PAX Unplugged, which runs from December 4 to 6, is available on the official convention website.
